stem.en: In a cell, the Golgi apparatus stops working while the ribosomes and ER stay healthy. Ravi says the cell will still send out its proteins as usual. Why is he wrong?

text.en: Ribosomes need the Golgi apparatus in order to start building any protein at all.

feedback.en: Ribosomes and ER are healthy here, so proteins are still made.

text.en: Proteins would be made in the nucleus instead, and they could not cross the nuclear pores.

feedback.en: Proteins are made on ribosomes, not in the nucleus.

text.en: The ER would dissolve, because it is held in place by the stacks of the Golgi apparatus.

feedback.en: Nothing in this case damages the ER, and the Golgi apparatus does not hold it in place.

text.en: Proteins are made but not packaged into vesicles.

explanation.en: The ribosomes and ER still make the protein, but the Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts and packages it into vesicles for secretion. Without that step the protein does not leave as usual.

hints.en: Which job does the Golgi apparatus do on the route out?
